---
title: "Bounded matrices"
---

Matrix values use `matrix([a,b],[c,d])`. They retain their type and rectangular
shape separately from ordinary lists. Dimensions are positive, each axis is at
most 16, and the matrix has at most 64 scalar entries. Ragged, empty, partially
filled and zero-dimensional matrices are rejected. Entries use the existing
bounded scalar parser; nested collections, equations and logical values are
outside this contract.

`AlgEquiv` checks dimensions and then corresponding scalar entries with the
existing algebraic equivalence machinery. `SameType` checks the supported matrix
type contract. `EqualComAss` preserves written arithmetic in corresponding
entries. Other matrix answer tests are rejected explicitly. Decimal literals and
author-value provenance follow the existing scalar rules. No algebraic set
matching or trig-set normalization policy changes are included.

Use native `<input><type>matrix</type>...` for an editor fixed to the evaluated
teacher answer's shape. Learner-selected dimensions use this explicit port
extension inside the input, shown in [the runnable example](../examples.qmd#bounded-matrix-input):

```xml
<matrix>
  <rows initial="2" min="1" max="4" resizable="1"/>
  <cols initial="2" min="1" max="4" resizable="1"/>
</matrix>
```

Each axis requires all four attributes; a fixed axis has `resizable="0"` and
equal `initial`, `min`, and `max`. The product of the two maxima must not exceed
64. This syntax is a STACK SymPy extension, not an assertion that native STACK
imports these extra elements.

Raw cells such as `x+x`, `0.1` and `1/2` remain unchanged in the editor. The
consumer serializes a matrix expression with each cell enclosed in parentheses
and lets its own parser interpret it. Empty cells remain invalid; resizing never
inserts numerical zeros. Surviving cells retain their raw values when resized.
The validation preview exposes the interpreted matrix before checking.

Editing, resizing, programmatic writes, resetting and changing variants invalidate
prior validation, grading and AI-feedback evidence. Reset returns the dimensions
and raw cells to their initial blank state. The editor presents input validity;
it does not infer cell, row, column or partial-credit grading. Authored PRTs remain
the only source of awarded scores.

The reusable editor is maintained in
[math-exercise](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/math-exercise), with standalone
`matrix-input.js` and `matrix-input.css`. STACK SymPy vendors audited commit
`f238da6d9a43d58d1fdf9ad592ac6223225268e0`; exact source links and SHA-256 checksums
are recorded in `_extensions/stack-sympy/vendor/matrix-input-provenance.json`.
No math-exercise Python checker or runtime is loaded, so each extension works
independently. Update by copying both standalone files from one audited upstream
commit, updating the manifest and rerunning matrix browser tests.

The component API is `MatrixInput.create({idPrefix, zeroDimensions, maxEntries,
labels, onChange})`, followed by `renderHTML(spec)` and `mount(wrapper)`.
`spec` contains `name`, `rows` and `cols`; each axis has `auto`, `initial`, `min`
and `max`. The mounted handle provides `read`, `write`, `resize`, `reset`,
`destroy` and `setState`. Read/write values are `{type:'matrix',rows,cols,raw}`
with raw strings in row-major order; notifications distinguish edits, resizes
and writes. STACK explicitly selects `zeroDimensions:'reject'` and `maxEntries:64`.
`setState` only displays supplied status and optional cell/row/column states;
consumers own all parsing and assessment policy.
